name: Trogir
title: Trogir Thickness Gauging | Ship UTM for Yard and Charter Craft
description: Ship thickness measurement in Trogir and Čiovo: ultrasonic hull and deck gauging for ferries, workboats, passenger vessels and ships in the Kaštela Bay area.
h1: Ship Hull and Deck Gauging in Trogir and on Čiovo Island
intro: Trogir is a small historic town on the Dalmatian coast, linked by a short channel to the island of Čiovo and close to the larger port of Split. Its waterfront serves ferries, passenger vessels, workboats and craft in for repair at a shipyard on the shore. Atlantis NDT sends ultrasonic gauging technicians from India to the vessel, alongside the quay, at a repair berth or at anchor in the bay.

highlights.h: A shipyard town on the Dalmatian coast
highlights.p: Trogir and the neighbouring island of Čiovo have shipbuilding and repair traditions, so vessels sometimes arrive for work and need gauging before, during or after their time on the slip.

highlights.h: Next door to the Split cargo port
highlights.p: Kaštela Bay is shared with Split, so a Trogir job can be combined with ships in the Split cargo port or at anchor in the bay under one planned mobilisation from India.
Most traffic is ferries, excursion boats, charter vessels and workboats of moderate size, so gauging tends to be about hull plating, decks and tank boundaries on smaller steel craft.

port.h: Trogir and the Čiovo channel: geography and waterfront
p: Trogir is built on a small island between the mainland and the larger island of Čiovo, joined to both by bridges. The old town is a protected historic site, and its seafront promenade is lined with moorings for yachts, excursion boats and passenger craft. Across the narrow channel, Čiovo's shoreline carries more industrial activity, including a shipyard and marine businesses. The approach from the open Adriatic runs through Kaštela Bay, a wide sheltered bay shared with the city of Split, and ships bound for Trogir pass many of the same navigational marks as ships heading to Split's cargo port.

Commercial shipping in Trogir itself is small in scale. Ferries serve nearby islands, and passenger vessels offer excursions along the coast. Charter fleets are based in the surrounding marinas, and workboats such as tugs, pilot craft and small supply vessels support yard and construction work around the bay. Larger cargo ships rarely call at Trogir, but many use the Split cargo terminals in the same bay, so Trogir is useful as a base for technicians who need to work across Kaštela Bay. The shared geography matters because a mobilisation from India is costly in effort, and clustering jobs in one area makes the trip more productive.

The channel and the harbour are shallow in places, so larger vessels stay clear and smaller ones berth where depth allows. The climate is Mediterranean, with hot summers and mild, wetter winters, and the summer months bring dense passenger traffic that limits berth availability and working windows. Winter is the practical season for most ship work, when excursion boats and ferries come off their routes for maintenance. The bora and jugo winds both affect the bay, and sudden gusts can make work on open decks or from launches impractical, so plans include a spare day for weather.

facilities.h: Where gauging can be carried out around Trogir
p: Facilities in Trogir are on a small scale, and we describe them generically rather than promise capacity. The shipyard on Čiovo and nearby marine businesses repair and refit small to medium steel and aluminium craft, and a vessel hauled out or on a slipway gives direct access to the underwater hull. The current status and capabilities of any yard should be confirmed with the owner and the agent when planning. Vessels too large for the local slips normally go to a yard in Split, Rijeka or elsewhere on the Adriatic for docking.

Away from the yard, gauging is done alongside. Ferries, excursion boats and workboats at the town quays or at a repair berth can have decks, ballast tanks, voids and engine room tank tops measured when they are idle. Larger ships anchored in Kaštela Bay, or berthed at Split, can be reached from Trogir by road or launch, which makes the town a convenient base. The agent or operator arranges quay access and boat transfers, and the work is scheduled around the vessel's maintenance programme.
list: Shipyard waterfront on Čiovo — hull plating, decks and tanks on vessels hauled out or alongside, subject to yard availability
Town quays — ferries and excursion boats gauged on decks, voids and ballast tanks during winter lay-up
Repair berths in the channel — workboats and tugs measured before and after steel renewal
Kaštela Bay anchorage — launch access for ships waiting for a Split berth or yard slot
Split cargo terminals nearby — bulk and general cargo ships gauged on the same mobilisation
Pre-docking visits — steel estimates for vessels that will go to a larger yard for a docking survey

context.h: Regulation and the Trogir maritime picture
p: Vessels calling at Trogir fall under Croatian port state control within the Paris MoU system, with the harbour master's authority for the Split-Dalmatia area handling inspections along this part of the coast. Domestic passenger vessels are surveyed under national rules that follow EU passenger ship safety requirements, so hull condition and watertight boundaries receive regular attention. Excursion vessels that carry many passengers in summer are a particular focus, and operators often commission gauging before their annual survey to avoid surprises.

EU rules also come into play. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on larger ships calling at EU ports, and the EU emissions rules reach ships above their size thresholds. For the small craft that dominate Trogir, steel condition matters more than carbon accounting: an owner deciding whether to renew plating or replace a boat wants measured numbers. The region's economy is strongly seasonal, with tourism driving the passenger fleet, so work is concentrated in the shoulder months, and early booking secures the best access.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Trogir
jobs.p: Trogir jobs involve smaller craft and are often combined with work in Split. An excursion operator might need hull and tank gauging before the season; a workboat owner might want a steel estimate before repairs on Čiovo; a ship waiting in Kaštela Bay might need a pre-purchase check. We agree scope and report format with the superintendent or owner before the team travels from India.
list: Pre-season hull and deck gauging on an excursion vessel at a town quay, with tank boundaries and engine room tank tops included
Steel estimate for a workboat before repairs on Čiovo, with readings taken on plating, frames and deck structure
Winter lay-up programme on an island ferry, covering vehicle deck, ramp hinges, voids and ballast tanks
Pre-purchase gauging of a small coaster at anchor in Kaštela Bay, accessed by launch through the agent
Combined mobilisation covering a Trogir workboat and a bulk carrier at the Split cargo terminals, with separate reports for each vessel

logistics: Split Airport lies very close to Trogir, between the town and the city, and offers seasonal European connections; Zagreb gives year-round links and a motorway to the coast. The agent or the operator arranges quay access and, where needed, a launch for vessels in the bay. The technicians travel from India on Schengen visas, so visa timing sets the earliest start. Combining Trogir with Split jobs can make better use of a single trip, and we plan the sequence once all dates are known.
vessels: Coasters at anchor in Kaštela Bay

faqs.q: Is there a shipyard in Trogir where docking work happens?
faqs.a: There is a shipyard on the Čiovo shore and other marine businesses nearby, but we do not rely on their capacity. The owner and the agent should confirm what the yard can take today. For larger vessels, a docking at Split, Rijeka or another Adriatic yard is more usual.

faqs.q: Can a Trogir job be combined with Split?
faqs.a: Yes. Trogir and Split share Kaštela Bay and the airport is between them, so we can plan one mobilisation that covers vessels in both places. Each ship gets its own report, and the sequence follows the access windows each operator provides.

faqs.q: When is the best time to gauge passenger vessels in Trogir?
faqs.a: Winter and early spring, when excursion boats and ferries are out of service. Summer berths are crowded and vessels run on tight schedules. Booking early secures access, and we agree which tanks and decks to open with the operator so the work finishes before the season starts.

faqs.q: Can aluminium craft be gauged as well as steel?
faqs.a: Yes. The gauge is calibrated on a block of the same alloy, and measurement points are chosen with the owner, because corrosion on light-alloy craft often concentrates near fittings and dissimilar-metal joints rather than across the whole plate.
